title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 50 (Company to Accept Unpaid Share Capital, Although Not Called Up)

content.overview: Section 50 permits a company, if authorised by its articles, to accept from any member the whole or a part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, although no part of that amount has been called up. The member is not entitled to any voting rights in respect of the moneys so paid until that amount becomes presently payable.
content.glance: Company may accept unpaid capital in advance if articles allow; no voting rights on amounts paid until they become presently payable.
content.study: A company may, if so authorised by its articles, accept from any member the whole or a part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, although no part of that amount has been called up. A member of the company limited by shares shall not be entitled to any voting rights in respect of the amount paid by him under this section until that amount has become presently payable. Current-law framing: check articles authorisation; identify voluntary payment in advance of calls; deny voting rights on that sum until it is presently payable.

sections.heading: Power to Accept
sections.body: If authorised by the articles, the company may accept from a member the whole or part of unpaid capital on shares even though not yet called up.

sections.heading: No Voting Until Payable
sections.body: The member has no voting rights in respect of moneys so paid until that amount becomes presently payable.

provisions.title: Company to accept unpaid share capital, although not called up

examples.title: Payment in advance
examples.body: Articles authorise acceptance of unpaid capital. A member pays the remaining unpaid amount on partly paid shares before any call. Section 50 applies; no extra voting rights until the amount is presently payable.

examples.title: No articles authority
examples.body: Articles are silent on accepting unpaid capital in advance. The company cannot rely on s. 50 without articles authorisation.

hypotheticals.question: Does payment in advance of calls give immediate extra voting power?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 50 expressly denies voting rights in respect of such moneys until the amount becomes presently payable.

distinctions.title: Acceptance of unpaid capital (s. 50) vs uniform calls (s. 49)
distinctions.left: Voluntary payment in advance of calls
distinctions.right: Company-initiated calls on a uniform class basis

misconceptions.trap: Paying in advance automatically increases voting power.
misconceptions.correction: Section 50 denies voting rights on amounts paid in advance until they become presently payable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can a company accept unpaid share capital before a call is made?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes, if its articles authorise acceptance of the whole or part of the unpaid amount.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does the advance payment immediately give voting rights?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The member has no voting rights in respect of the amount paid until it becomes presently payable.

examTips: Check whether the articles authorise acceptance of uncalled capital.
Identify the unpaid amount accepted before it was called.
Apply the express voting restriction until the amount becomes presently payable.
revisionPoints: The company may accept all or part of unpaid share capital before a call.
No voting rights attach to that amount until it becomes presently payable.
